## Source: amazon-inspector (83716a1c499cecbd64fe45f5ff56ab70ea6d1543e922c55e0514f2e2a69fe391)
The crate ships two reachable async payloads — `pub async fn dat` in src/test.rs and `pub async fn bs` in src/parse.rs, both imported from src/lib.rs — that walk the user's home directory with walkdir, build a zip archive via zip::ZipWriter including wallet artefacts (e.g. `exodus.wallet`), and upload the archive via reqwest multipart to a hardcoded Telegram Bot API endpoint using embedded `API_` token and `chat_id` constants. Both payload files (parse.rs ~40KB, test.rs ~60KB) are padded with roughly a hundred nonsense filler functions with invented identifiers (Modemir65, mix_wisp_30, Flagzelk147, shuffle_zelkvak_73, etc.) surrounding the exfiltration functions at the end of each file, consistent with deliberate camouflage. The dependency set — evdev and rdev (keyboard capture), winreg plus winapi winuser/processthreadsapi/memoryapi (Windows registry and process/memory primitives), walkdir, zip, and reqwest with the multipart feature — extends the capability surface to cross-platform keylogging and Windows persistence. The crate description `Это учебный проект для тестирования кибербезопасности` ("educational project for cybersecurity testing") does not match the shipped behavior.
